doc.title: John Levy interviewed by Monk Rowe, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995

title: Learning the touring system and Wes Montgomery's customs story
summary: Levy learned international promoters and border rules with Shearing; he relays Wes Montgomery's guitar inspection in Spain and Rowe's parallel Ruth Brown story.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Yeah. So I’ll have to tackle that when I get back. And I learned a lot of things, a lot about the system by working, by my experiences with George Shearing at the beginning and traveling in Europe and Japan and all of that. You’ve got to know all of the different promoters all over the world and you’ve got to know the system, how you go about getting in and out of countries. And Wes Montgomery tells a story about, I wasn’t with them and he went to Spain. And he got off the plane and the guy said to him, “you a guitar player?” He said, “yeah.” So he said they took the guitar out and looked in it and looked in the case and everything. And they had these dogs sniffing for dope. And he was

there and the guy said to him, the head of customs, he said, “so you’re supposed to be able to play this thing, now play something.” So he says, “you know it has to be hooked up.” He tried to explain to the guy. The guy said “play.” And so he had to take the guitar out and play something to show that he—
Ruth Brown told us a similar story but it was in the south with a policeman on the side of the road.
Oh yeah. They had— the musicians had some great experiences with that kind of system in the south and what would happen to you in that instance you know.
